edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia (archive bub_gb_DY2xvRwPetMC), Latin column, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. VII, printed pp. 4-5 (PDF pp. 28-29)

source_text: Si quis dicit Christum salvum factum esse, et non confitetur ipsum esse salvatorem mundi, ac lucem mundi, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Quo pacto potest quispiam dicere, Christum salvum esse factum? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Ego sum vita. Et: Ego veni, ut vitam habeant. Et: qui credit in me mortem non videbit; sed videbit vitam aeternam.
thought_title: Christ is the Savior, not one who was saved
orientation: Gregory condemns saying that Christ was saved, since he is the Savior and the life of the world.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says Christ [was] made safe (salvum factum esse), and does not confess him to be the savior (salvatorem) of the world, and light (lucem) of the world, as it is written; let him be anathema. By what means (quo pacto) can anyone say Christ was made safe? when the Lord himself says: I am the life (vita). And: I came, that they may have life. And: who believes (credit) in me will not see death (mortem); but will see eternal life (vitam aeternam).

choices.why: Made safe, delivered: the claim that Christ himself needed saving.

bible_refs.note: quoted: Ego veni, ut vitam habeant
composite saying: qui credit in me ... vitam aeternam

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ was saved, and does not confess that he is the Savior of the world (John 4:42) and the light of the world (John 8:12), as it is written, let him be anathema.

How can anyone say that Christ was saved, when the Lord himself says, “I am the life” (John 11:25); and, “I came that they may have life” (John 10:10); and, “Whoever believes in me will not see death, but will see eternal life” (John 8:51; John 6:47)?
notes: Salvum factum esse rendered “was saved” (made safe, delivered).

“Savior of the world” is the wording of John 4:42; the margin sigla point to John 3 (3:17) and to Isaiah 42 and 49 for the light (Isaiah 42:6; 49:6, “a light to the nations”); the wording here is John's, so the Isaiah passages are not cited inline.
“I am the life” also stands in John 14:6.
The last saying is a composite: “will not see death” (John 8:51) with “whoever believes in me has eternal life” (John 6:47; compare John 3:36, 11:26).
